checks.title: BNotK 2007 activity report to Justice Ministry, dated 14 July 2008
checks.locator: Physical/printed pp. 5–6, section B.III.1–2; cover date p. 1
checks.read_extent: Read cover and complete relevant early electronic commercial-register transmission discussion, not all 25 pages.
checks.result: The contemporary report describes expected initial difficulties and prior EGVP outages in individual Länder, including at lower load. It reports precautionary fallback submissions for 31 August 2007 and says disturbances that day were apparently avoided. This supports historical existence of outages/concern, but EGVP submission transport is not identical to register query servers and no frequency/cause series establishes frequent early commercial-register server overload.
checks.short_excerpt: Technische Störungen des EGVP zum 31. August 2007 konnten auf diese Weise – soweit ersichtlich – vermieden werden.
checks.access: Official primary PDF read through web extraction; no local original retained.
checks.temporal_limit: Contemporary 2007/2008 evidence predates response; scope and successful mitigation preserved.

checks.title: BVerfG 28 August 2000, 1 BvR 1307/91, press access to land registers
checks.locator: Official indexed reasoning on legitimate interest, press freedom and personality rights
checks.read_extent: Read relevant official indexed paragraphs and case setting; direct original HTML returned 403, so no claim to complete judgement review.
checks.result: The balancing of personal-data protection against legitimate access supports treating broad but qualified access separately from unrestricted publicity. The DAV request to change displayed personal fields is a legislative preference; neither this old case nor a commercial-register case establishes that its proposed reform is legally impossible or that current GBV automatically violates GDPR.
checks.access: Direct original 403 is an explicit limit; indexed official text only.
checks.temporal_limit: Predates response/GDPR; used only for constitutional access distinction, not a new GDPR merits decision.
